title_as_printed: Solubility of methane in the fermentation media of methanotrophs bacteria
pressure_note: atmospheric pressure in the cell (gas pre-saturated with water vapour, total pressure adjusted to atmospheric); col 'L2,1(T,P)' is the Ostwald coefficient at this experimental pressure; mole fraction column is at gas partial pressure 101.325 kPa (derived by authors)

value.what: Ostwald coefficient L=c_liquid/c_vapour at equilibrium (eq. 10), directly from the measured gas volume

value2.what: mole fraction of methane in liquid at gas partial pressure 101.325 kPa, calculated by the authors from the Henry coefficient (iterative procedure)

composition.other_species: aqueous fermentation medium of methane-utilizing bacteria (Table 1A, concentrations in g/dm3: MgSO4 1, CaCl2 0.05, KNO3 1, Na2MoO4.2H2O printed 5.54 (sic, as printed in Table 1A), FeEDTA solution, trace elements, phosphate stock Na2HPO4+KH2PO4); very dilute, treated as water by the authors; not mappable to the six-ion set without conversion

extra_unmapped: L2,1 inf (T,Ps,1) (Ostwald coefficient at infinite dilution, calculated)
10^-9 H2,1(T,Ps,1)/Pa (Henry coefficient at solvent vapour pressure, calculated by authors from eq. 12)
conversion_needs: Ostwald coefficient definition needs the vapour-phase concentration (ideal-gas assumption used by authors)
notes: Fermentation medium, five temperatures; same conventions as Table 2.
